(high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongosync/current/reference/api/resume.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongosync/current/faq.md

evidence.quote: When you send a `resume` request, `mongosync` might take at least two minutes before resuming the migration.
Starting in `mongosync` 1.7.3, `mongosync` can take at least two minutes to respond when you resume or restart a sync operation.

During this time, any calls to the [`progress`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongosync/current/reference/api/progress.md#std-label-c2c-api-progress) endpoint might fail. If a `progress` call fails, it is safe to retry.

statements.statement: The resume API warns of at least two minutes before migration resumes.
The FAQ dates this behavior to 1.7.3.
Progress calls can temporarily fail and may safely be retried.
statements.note: FAQ says progress calls might fail and are safe to retry.

edits.rationale: The resume API page warns mongosync might take at least two minutes before resuming. The FAQ dates the behavior to mongosync 1.7.3 and says progress calls may fail and are safe to retry. Both pages together establish every statement.

edits.old: Recovery depends on source oplog retention. If a source outage exceeds the oplog window, MongoDB requires restarting the migration from the beginning, removing migrated destination data. Mafiree separately recommends increasing the source oplog before a long pause. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)
edits.new: Recovery depends on source oplog retention. If a source outage exceeds the oplog window, MongoDB requires restarting the migration from the beginning, removing migrated destination data. MongoDB's oplog sizing documentation advises increasing the source cluster's oplog size (oplogSizeMB) if you plan to pause synchronization for an extended period. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongosync/current/reference/mongosync-behavior.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongosync/current/reference/oplog-sizing.md

evidence.quote: If the source cluster outage exceeds the [oplog window](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongosync/current/reference/oplog-sizing.md#std-label-c2c-oplog-sizing), `mongosync` cannot resume.

Use the [`oplogSizeMB`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-replication.oplogSizeMB) setting to increase the size of the `oplog` on the source cluster.

statements.statement: If a source outage exceeds the oplog window, MongoDB requires restarting the migration from the beginning, removing migrated destination data.
statements.note: Stated in the behavior page warning.

statements.statement: Mafiree separately recommends increasing the source oplog before a long pause.
statements.note: No Mafiree source found. MongoDB's own oplog sizing page gives this advice, so the advice is supported but not the Mafiree attribution.

edits.old: Mongosync does not automatically restart after errors. Its FAQ recommends a script or process manager such as systemd; RightTouch's migration ran the worker under systemd, illustrating external process supervision. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)
edits.new: Mongosync does not automatically restart after errors. Its FAQ recommends writing a script or using an operating system process manager such as systemd to restart the process. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongosync/current/faq.md

evidence.quote: `mongosync` does not automatically restart on error. However, you can write a script or use your operating system's process managers, `systemd` for example, to restart the `mongosync` process.
